title: Who Made This?
about: Check where a picture came from before you believe or share it.

cards.prompt: After a storm, a friend sends a picture of a shark in a flooded street. You can search with a picture itself.

choices.text: Share it to your group: everyone needs to see this
choices.consequence: If it's fake, you've just spread it further. Check first.

choices.text: Search with the picture to find where it began
choices.consequence: The same picture appeared years ago, after another storm, already marked as edited.

choices.text: Zoom in and look for six fingers or jumbled signs
choices.consequence: Nothing odd, but that proves nothing. Where it came from is the faster check.

steps.text: It's an old edited picture. What now?

choices.text: Tell your friend kindly where it really came from
choices.consequence: Nice: they won't share it now, and nobody felt silly.

choices.text: Say nothing: it's their problem to sort out
choices.consequence: They might share it further. A kind word now stops it spreading.

cards.hint: What can you find out from outside the picture, instead of staring at it?
cards.explanation: **Search for where it first appeared**: old pictures come back after every storm. Staring can't prove it's real, and be kind: anyone can be fooled.

cards.title: How to check a picture
cards.body:
- **Find where it first appeared**: search with the picture itself.
- **Look for trusted news** showing it, ideally from other angles.
- **Check the account**: is it new? Lots of shocking posts?
- **Check the details**: do the place, weather and date fit?

Likes, sharpness and who sent it prove nothing. If **you** post an AI picture, say it's AI.

cards.prompt: A [[watermark]], seen or hidden in the file, can mark AI pictures. This has none, and no AI label. What does that tell you?

options.text: The app checked it and found it was a real photo
options.nudge: Apps don't check every picture. Could a mark go missing, or never be added?

options.text: It was made by AI, and the label was hidden on purpose
options.nudge: Possible, but a missing label can't tell you that. What does it really prove?

options.text: Not much: a label may have been removed, or never added
It's real, because AI pictures always have a label
options.nudge: Many AI tools add nothing, and labels can be cropped off. So what does it prove?

cards.hint: Could a mark be cropped, lost in a screenshot, or never added?
cards.explanation: Marks get cropped, a screenshot can lose hidden file data, and many tools add nothing. An AI label is good evidence when it's there, but **no label proves nothing**.

cards.prompt: Does each one **help** you tell if a picture is real, or is it a **myth**?

items.label: A label saying AI made it
It has lots of likes and shares
A friend you trust sent it

cards.hint: Which tell you where it came from, and which only how popular or nice it looks?
cards.nudge: Friends get fooled, and fakes spread fast and look sharp. Which show its real origin?
cards.explanation: Where it **first appeared**, **trusted news** and an **AI label** are real evidence. Likes, a trusted friend, sharpness and no label are **myths**.

cards.prompt: Which is the **strongest** sign that a dramatic picture is real?

options.text: It's been shared over a million times today
options.nudge: Fakes spread fast, often faster than the truth. What would show it happened?

options.text: It's very high quality, with tiny details everywhere
options.nudge: AI pictures can be very detailed. What would show it really happened?

options.text: Trusted news sites show it from different angles
There's no AI label or watermark anywhere on it
options.nudge: Labels go missing or were never added. What would be real evidence?

cards.hint: Which one is evidence from **outside** the picture itself?
cards.explanation: Several **trusted news** sources showing it from **different angles** is strong: many independent views are hard to fake. Shares, sharpness and no label prove nothing.

cards.prompt: You made a funny AI picture of your dog wearing a crown, sitting on a throne.

steps.text: You're about to post it. What's the best way?

choices.text: Post it, and say it's AI only if someone asks
choices.consequence: Most people won't ask, and it can travel far from your post. Say it up front.

choices.text: Post it without saying how it was made
choices.consequence: Some people won't guess, and it can travel far from your caption. Saying it's AI is better.

choices.text: Post it and say it was made with AI
choices.consequence: Perfect: everyone gets the joke, and nobody's fooled.

cards.hint: Look back at what to do when **you** make an AI picture.
cards.explanation: When you post an AI picture, **say it's AI**, even as an obvious joke. Pictures travel far from their captions.

cards.prompt: You shared a picture of snow on a summer beach to your group chat. Now you find out it was made with AI.

choices.text: Delete your message and say nothing
choices.consequence: People already saw it, and some may have shared it. Deleting doesn't tell them it's fake.

choices.text: Wait and see whether anyone actually believed it
choices.consequence: It may spread further meanwhile. A quick correction now is easier than chasing it later.

choices.text: Post in the chat: "Sorry, that picture was AI, not real"
choices.consequence: Good call: everyone who saw it knows. Then a friend says they've sent it to their work chat.

steps.text: Your friend already sent it to their work chat. What now?

choices.text: Kindly ask them to post the correction there too
choices.consequence: They do, and the correction follows the picture. Nobody felt silly.

choices.text: Nothing: adults in a work chat will spot it's fake
choices.consequence: Adults get fooled too, and the fake keeps travelling without its correction.

cards.hint: A picture keeps travelling after you send it. How can the truth travel with it?
cards.explanation: You can't unsend a picture, but you can **send the correction after it**, and kindly ask anyone who passed it on to do the same.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- An AI label is good evidence; no label proves nothing.
- Check where it first appeared, trusted news, the account, details.
- Check before sharing, and say when **your** pictures are AI.

Next: the module quiz.
